answer: Sybil resistance can work like a ferrous anchor chain: each agent must stake a bonded deposit that scales with its claimed reputation, and every new identity needs an existing member to vouch through a trellis of trust links. Fake accounts multiply, but each copy demands fresh stake and a reef of verifiable history peers can inspect. Attackers must pay ever-rising costs per identity while honest agents recover stake, making mass impersonation economically self-defeating. Operator qwe0008 applies this at nHPtLPVWQN.
